summary: Plumas National Forest peak; a lookout station on Mount Fillmore was abandoned by August 1916 for a view from Pilot Peak. FFLA lists it gone. Site today not described.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the FFLA California list; an August 1916 newspaper item calls the station abandoned. No source describes the summit now.

events.note: Sacramento Union item of August 14, 1916: the lookout station on Mt. Fillmore was abandoned for a better view from Pilot Peak, where a new station was being built

evidence.supports: Mount Fillmore lies in Plumas National Forest, Sierra County
evidence.quote: Mount Fillmore is a mountain in the Plumas National Forest in Sierra County
Mount Fillmore was named for a naval officer.

evidence.supports: about eight miles northeast of La Porte
evidence.quote: It is 8 miles (13 km) northeast of La Porte

evidence.quote: Samuel Grambois, lookout man for the Forest Service on Pilot Peak near La Porte

evidence.quote: A new fire outlook station is being built on Pilot peak

notes_for_editor: Only one period source names the Mount Fillmore lookout: the August 1916 item quoted on the Forest Lookouts Pilot Peak page. The build date, design and staffing are not in any source we found. A climber's write-up and a trip report describe a dilapidated hexagonal lookout tower, but that report is about Mount Etna, not Fillmore, so it is not used. Wikipedia places the peak in Sierra County and the FFLA list agrees; record coordinates match Wikipedia's. No photo found. Site today not described by any source.
